proposed.sourceName: Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS) — Fatwa Committee ruling on Ethanol
proposed.paraphrase: The MUIS Fatwa Committee permits ethanol (natural or synthetic, not derived from khamr) used exclusively as a solvent/carrier for food flavourings, provided the ethanol in the flavouring does not exceed 0.5% and in the final product does not exceed 0.1% — i.e. below intoxicating levels.

proposed.sourceName: Fatawa Center — 'Is Vanilla Extract Halal if it Contains Alcohol?' (Dr. Mahmoud A. Omar, Al-Azhar Fatwa Council member)
proposed.paraphrase: Holds vanilla extract containing alcohol permissible per many contemporary scholars when the alcohol is only a non-khamr solvent present in residual, non-intoxicating amounts and the product is used in cooking/baking (judged by intended use, maqasid, with reference to AAOIFI Shariah Standard 18), while noting a stricter minority that deems any added ethyl alcohol impermissible regardless of quantity. (Standing fatwa, accessed 2026-07-01.)

researcherNote: vanilla extract seeded general grade 3 (contested). MUIS permits carriers only up to 0.5% (which vanilla extract (~35% ethanol, non-khamr) does not automatically satisfy) and Fatawa Center records a stricter minority deeming any added ethyl alcohol impermissible — a genuine dispute. Two independent tier-1. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01 (batch pre-approval).
